item.title: Malaysia to integrate water pricing into national adaptation plan, says environment ministry
item.description: The impacts of deforestation must also be counted towards the true cost of water, the ministry’s secretary-general said. The country's first fair share carbon budget report could help strengthen the government’s forest conservation efforts.

item.title: Thailand's decarbonisation ambition deserves a bond to match
item.description: As Asean's first government to issue a sustainability-linked bond, Thailand could innovate further by linking fixed income instruments to decarbonisation using "transition linkers". Yet this must be matched by policy credibility.

item.title: Global plastic demands could more than double by 2050 despite harm evidence: study
item.description: The plastics boom is being driven by fossil fuel and petrochemical giants banking on rising production of packaging, including for ready meals, found a new Greenpeace report.

item.title: Asia Pacific insurers warn climate shocks are becoming a systemic financial threat
item.description: Insurance companies increasingly worry that escalating climate extremes could destabilise financial systems, not their balance sheets – an anxiety felt acutely in Asia Pacific, a MSCI study finds.

item.title: South Korea, Singapore sign pact to study small modular reactors
item.description: Deal marks first nuclear MOU between KHNP and Singapore agency as city-state explores low-carbon power options.

item.title: Homestead farming is empowering Indigenous women in central India
item.description: Women in Mandla, Madhya Pradesh are becoming leaders of their homestead farms.

item.title: Game on: How math can help design strategies for climate crisis, diplomacy
item.description: Evolutionary game theory is useful to devise strategies for real-life situations such as international negotiations and ecological crises, where players are unequal, and choices are complex.

item.title: Resorts World Sentosa sustainability lead departs for Macao casino brand SJM
item.description: Brian Ho has left the Singapore casino operator after a year as vice president of sustainability and joined SJM Resorts in Macao in an equivalent role. RWS has replaced Ho with his predecessor Loh Su Kim.

item.title: ‘Wake-up call’ for Asean energy security as Singapore, Thailand face Iran war's LNG risks
item.description: Long-term energy security is also a concern for Malaysia, the Philippines and Vietnam, which have been expanding LNG infrastructure. Experts say that a shift to renewables is worthwhile, but policies are diverging across the region.

item.title: Rethinking Malaysia’s path to net zero
item.description: Carbon credits to be tabled under Malaysia’s new climate change bill should serve as a bridge towards decarbonisation rather than a substitute for it.
